title: The Billion-Dollar Debt Trap

beats.say: One famous author holds $1 billion in debt and calls it a winning strategy.
beats.visual: Cinematic shot of a man's hands in a dark suit holding a pen over a massive stack of loan documents, dramatic side lighting.

beats.say: But the system he used to escape the rat race has a hidden trap.
beats.visual: A close-up of a vintage rat running on a metal wheel, dark moody background, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: He divides debt into two categories: things that pay you, and things that cost you.
beats.visual: A heavy iron scale balancing a green ledger on one side and a stack of luxury shopping bags on the other.

beats.say: Bad debt buys cars and clothes that lose value the second you swipe your card.
beats.visual: The back of a luxury sports car driving down a wet city street at night, neon lights reflecting on the pavement.

beats.say: Good debt buys assets like real estate, using other people's money to build your wealth.
beats.visual: A low-angle shot of a classic brick apartment building under a gloomy sky, warm light coming from a few windows.

beats.say: This is called financial leverage, and the math looks incredibly simple on paper.
beats.visual: Hands spinning a high-end architectural model of a skyscraper, moody architectural studio setting.

beats.say: But here's the part the gurus leave out: leverage works both ways.
beats.visual: A dramatic shot of a close-up of a sharp metal blade reflecting light, dark background.

beats.say: Imagine buying a $100,000 property with $20,000 down. That's 5x leverage.
beats.visual: A hand putting a single stack of $100 bills on a clean wooden table next to a tiny house model.

beats.say: If the market goes up 20%, you double your money before fees.
beats.visual: A close-up of a green graph line rising on a dark glass surface, out of focus city lights in the background.

beats.say: But if the property price drops just 20%, your entire down payment is wiped out.
beats.visual: A hand knocking over a small house model on a dark table, pieces scattering, high contrast lighting.

beats.say: In 2012, even his own company filed for bankruptcy after a $23.7 million court ruling.
beats.visual: A vintage metal bankruptcy court sign mounted on a dark marble wall, moody lighting.

beats.say: Debt is a power tool, not a safety net. Follow us to learn the rules...
beats.visual: A close-up of a hand holding a heavy steel wrench on a dark industrial workbench.

beats.say: ...of the money game school never taught you, especially when you realize that...
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person looking out of a high-rise office window at a sprawling city at dusk.

caption: Debt can build empires or crush them. Here is the math of leverage they never taught you in school. #personalfinance #debtfree #investing #moneyrules #financialliteracy
description: An analysis of good debt versus bad debt, using the math of financial leverage. While borrowing to buy assets can accelerate wealth, a small market drop can wipe out your entire investment.
first_comment: Would you ever use 5x leverage to buy an asset, or is the risk too high?

facts.claim: One famous author holds $1 billion in debt and calls it a winning strategy.
facts.basis: Robert Kiyosaki self-reported having over $1 billion in debt in January 2024.

facts.claim: A $100,000 property bought with $20,000 down is 5x leverage.
facts.basis: Fact sheet leverage math: $100,000 property with $20,000 down is 5x leverage.
